I hit a syntax error, so I need to redo this cleanly. I'm working out the perpendicular distance from the camera position to the west wall plane at x=-3.93, accounting for the viewing direction.

With heading 270 the forward vector points in -x, so image row for the floor depends only on depth D=px+3.93, giving a constant junction row across all columns. Testing this against frames 179 and 181, the computed junction rows (316 and 333) line up with observed floor color transitions, confirming the formula. But then I notice one measured region has its bottom edge above that junction row, meaning it can't be sitting on the floor — it must be an elevated object instead.

Working out its height at the wall plane for both frames, I get top heights around z=1.29-1.32 and bottom heights around z=0.15-0.26, which are consistent between frames but don't quite reach the floor (z=0) if it's mounted flush against the wall, suggesting it's actually positioned slightly forward of the wall rather than on it.

Computing the wall-plane positions for f179 and f181 gives inconsistent x/y coordinates, so the object isn't actually sitting on that plane. I need to switch to bearing-only triangulation instead, using two poses with different camera x-positions but the same height, and setting up the ratio equations relating pixel offset to the object's true y and x position.

Solving for x using the two bearing equations gives x ≈ -1.909, then plugging back gives y ≈ 3.394, but this feels off so I should double check the setup.

Let me try a different pairing, using f180's center estimate (x=-1.326) against f179 — the results don't line up well, suggesting the group centers themselves may be shifting between frames due to changing mask edges. Reconsidering the geometry, if this is a fixed object like wooden_chair_1 moving west relative to the camera, decreasing distance would spread the bearing angles, so I should revisit which object this actually corresponds to.

Also checking the lower brown group across f180/f181 — the back-projections land consistently around (-3.12, 3.40) with ztop 0.66 in both frames, about 0.35m from the chair's back position. That consistency across frames suggests this could be the same chair's seat or legs rather than a separate object.

Maybe these are two separate brown objects rather than one chair, with the upper one's floor contact hidden behind the lower object. Considering the upper group's width (~1.0m) and height (~1.14m), it seems too large to just be a chair back component.

Reconsidering, this could be a wall-mounted item or a wooden door/cabinet against the west wall instead. Let me triangulate using the left edge of the upper group across frames 179-181, tracking u-values 318, 338, 355 and converting to r and pixel-x coordinates to solve for the object's actual x-position.

The two frame pairs give inconsistent x-estimates (-1.31 vs -0.37), suggesting this left edge isn't a fixed feature but likely an occlusion boundary that shifts with viewpoint. I'm now checking the right edge instead, using u-values 361, 379, 404 to see if it produces a more consistent triangulation.

The right edge triangulates consistently to about (-2.44, 4.01), with two independent frame pairs agreeing closely -- this looks like a genuine 3D feature. Comparing it against wooden_chair_1's known position at (-2.83, 3.57) gives a distance of roughly 0.57 m, so I'm checking whether floor_lamp_1 is a better match instead.

The x-coordinate lines up but the y is off by 1.84 m, which rules out the lamp; a chair corner near (-2.6, 3.8) given the chair's ~0.5m width would plausibly land close to this point, so I'm leaning toward attributing it to the chair despite the offset. I want to also triangulate the lower brown group, which showed consistent floor contact around (-3.12, 3.40).

The lower group doesn't appear separately in frame 179 — it's likely merged with the upper brown region since they'd overlap at that viewpoint. Since the predicted chair position falls within that merged range and the floor solution is only 0.33m from the mapped chair, I suspect both groups belong to wooden_chair_1, though the mapped position might need a slight refinement toward (-3.0, 3.45). Still, I want to be careful here — with 19 frames remaining, it's worth moving closer to the chair region for a cleaner look rather than relying on this triangulation.

I estimate the chair sits around (-2.9, 3.5) while I'm currently at (1.202, 1.899) facing west; turning roughly 21° would point me toward it. Rather than that precise pivot, I could just continue west and capture views along the way, using my remaining frames to also cover the SW quadrant and the open floor area near the center.

I remember noting the south half was already swept, though the blue vase near (-2.45, 1.50) sits in that SW-ish region, so I want to double check there aren't unmapped objects there while confirming the chair's exact position. My plan is to take three more westward steps of about 0.75 each, landing near x≈-1.05, then turn to scan south/southwest before approaching the chair directly.

Combining the floor-contact reading from two poses at (-3.12, 3.40) with the right-edge triangulation at (-2.44, 4.01), the chair's footprint works out to roughly 0.68 x 0.61 meters, centered around (-2.78, 3.70).

That matches the mapped position of (-2.83, 3.57) almost exactly, confirming wooden_chair_1 — I'll set it at (-2.82, 3.60) with confidence 0.95, no new object needed here.

Checking a few other candidate points now: one out at (-4.14, 8.58) is beyond the walls, so that's likely a wall gradient artifact I should ignore, while another dark region gives a depth reading around 2.96m near (-0.26,...).

Working through the plant's predicted pixel position across frames, I'm getting the u-coordinate landing just off the right edge of the frame (588 vs the 511 limit), close enough to the observed green region at 478-511 to still count as the plant near the edge.

At f181, the plant should be behind the camera given the geometry, matching the absence of green. So I'll proceed with three more westward moves — checking that the path from x=1.202 to x=-1.048 doesn't intersect the chair at (-2.8,3.6), though the blue vase at (-2.45,1.50) is close to the travel line at y=1.9, so I'll note that but still stop at -1.048.
answer: West-wall junction rows confirm the poses (f179 vj=316 observed 316; f181 vj=333 observed 333). Triangulating the upper brown region's right edge across two independent pose pairs gives (−2.46, 4.02) and (−2.43, 4.00), while the lower brown group's floor contact agrees at (−3.14, 3.39)/(−3.11, 3.40). Those bracket a 0.68 × 0.61 m footprint centred (−2.78, 3.70) — wooden_chair_1, seat plus back, not a new object.
